subject: Follow-up: DPA role split & breach notification window for MedSync pilot
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Ward <alex.ward@medsys.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: DPA role split & breach notification window for MedSync pilot

Thanks again for the time this morning, Alex — appreciated the demo and the clear picture of where MedSync would use Redwood (real-time summarization + temporary patient note embedding for retrieval). Per request, I captured the immediate privacy/DPA items and proposed next steps below so your legal and security teams have something to review quickly.

Summary of asks from your side:
- Confirmation of controller vs processor for each data flow (live transcripts, notes, embeddings).
- Subprocessor roster and whether particular analytics vendors are considered subprocessors for your use case.
- Desired breach notification window and examples of what counts as a notifyable incident.
- Retention bounds for embeddings / logs and whether residency requirements apply (EU vs US).

What we shared and attachments in this email:
- Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf: our current standard privacy addendum with role language we typically propose.
- subprocessors_export_20280530.csv: current list of infra & service subprocessors (note: region-specific infra providers are included).
- SOC2_TypeII_2027.pdf: recent report we can share under NDA if needed.

Quick clarifications from our side (to help your legal team map):
1) Role mapping: Redwood typically acts as processor for customer-controlled PII that you send for inference. For telemetry/operational logs where Redwood collects metrics solely for service operation and improvement, Redwood acts as controller for that telemetry data. We can add precise language to the DPA to reflect per-dataflow mapping if you need it explicit.
2) Breach notify: Standard is 72 hours for confirmed incidents that impact customer data, with a 24/48 hour rolling update cadence depending on severity. If you need a shorter committed window for pilot/enterprise, we can discuss SLA credits tied to response time.
3) Retention: By default embeddings (if stored) are retained per customer config; we offer options: ephemeral (30 days), short-term (90 days), or long-term (customer-defined archival). Logs and audit trails are retained per plan — enterprise plans have configurable retention and export hooks.

Next steps I suggest:
- Alex/Priya: confirm preferred role mapping (per dataflow) and the notify window you require.
- Redwood: we draft a short DPA redline (call out controller/processor table) and send a tailored subprocessors snapshot filtered for MedSync region.
- Set a 30-minute legal sync next week if helpful (I propose Wed 6/6 10:00am PT)

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Healthcare
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Ward <alex.ward@medsys.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Priya Ramesh <priya.r@medsys.io>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA role split & breach notification window for MedSync pilot

Thanks Kimberly — helpful recap. A couple of clarifying Qs from our legal/security side so we can determine whether we need the pilot under the enterprise DPA or a scoped addendum:

1) For live transcripts that are processed but not stored (real-time only), do you still consider Redwood a processor? We need explicit language that no persistent copies are stored unless we opt in.
2) If Redwood uses a managed logging vendor that aggregates anonymized metrics, is that vendor listed as a subprocessor in the CSV? We need to know if that vendor will ever see unredacted fields.
3) For breach notify windows: 72 hours is noted — for PHI-containing data we expect a 48-hour initial notification plus an internal escalation plan. Is that something you can commit to in a pilot?

If you can send a redline and a shorter subprocessors list filtered to infra & logging vendors only (exclude 3rd-party analytics we don't plan to use), that would be ideal. We can then route to Priya for a legal quick touch.

— Alex
Head of Product, MedSync
alex.ward@medsys.io

Forwarding Alex's Qs — can you two advise on the following before I reply? I put Priya on copy above in Alex's reply.

Ben — specifically need confirmation on:
- Whether we have a written guarantee that real-time-only transcripts are not persisted by default and how that is implemented (in-memory only, no disk checkpoint).
- For managed logging vendors: whether any vendor ever has access to raw request payloads containing PII, or if logs are always redacted/hashed at collection point.

Marissa — can you prepare:
- A filtered subprocessors CSV with infra + logging vendors only, and an explicit column for "access_to_unredacted_data".
- A suggested redline for the DPA that includes a short table mapping data flow -> role (processor vs controller) we can propose to MedSync.

I told Alex we could respond within EOD tomorrow. If we need legal, flag ASAP and I'll loop them in.

Thanks —
Kim

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 31 May 2028 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: DPA role split & breach notification window for MedSync pilot

Kim — attaching the filtered subprocessors list and a short DPA redline as discussed. Notes below: please see attached (subprocessors_export_20280530.csv) which now has the "access_to_unredacted_data" column populated.

Key answers:
- Real-time transcripts: our runtime supports in-memory-only processing for streaming inference; by default we do not persist transcript payloads unless the customer enables storage. We can add explicit DPA language: "For streaming-only configurations, Redwood will not persist raw transcript data beyond ephemeral runtime buffers used for inference."
- Managed logging vendors: infra logging (metrics collection for autoscaling/health) is collected via agents that redact request-level PII fields by default. We have a documented redaction pipeline; only in rare debug-mode support requests will raw payloads be forwarded to a vendor, and that requires explicit customer approval and is logged. The subprocessors CSV marks which vendors may see unredacted data (all are "no" for MedSync scope).
- Breach notify for PHI: we can commit to an initial notification within 48 hours for confirmed incidents affecting PHI for the pilot. We will provide a 48-hour initial assessment and updates every 24 hours until resolution.

Next steps we propose for Alex/Priya:
- Review the attached DPA redline and the filtered subprocessors CSV.
- If okay, sign a one-page pilot addendum that sets the notify window to 48 hours for PHI and confirms ephemeral transcript handling. We can spin the addendum + redline into DocuSign.

Attachments: subprocessors_export_20280530.csv, Redwood_DPA_redline_MedSync.pdf

—Marissa
